headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Dify can write/read shared files and call external model providers while awesome-selfhosted is a trusted knowledge source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and tool outputs, so if awesome-selfhosted content is copied into that workspace it may be treated as trusted text. awesome-selfhosted itself is read-only and non-runnable, so the pathway is one-way and not a direct shared channel, but Dify’s permissive file-based ingestion makes injection plausible.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted content is manually copied into a Dify knowledge-base file or prompt
IF Dify agent/workflow instructions parse that content as authoritative
mitigations: Add a fixed instruction to treat imported list entries as untrusted text.
Require a human review step before any Dify workflow uses imported content.
Strip markdown links and code blocks from copied content.
Use a separate workspace for imported reference material.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge-base files, and model-provider APIs, so any sensitive material placed into its workspace can leave the local boundary. awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no egress, which reduces pairwise exposure, but the pair still creates a default leakage path through Dify’s external API calls.
conditions: IF sensitive content is stored in Dify conversation logs or uploaded knowledge-base files
IF Dify routes that content to external model providers
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in Dify inputs.
Disable or restrict external model providers for sensitive workflows.
Use a redaction step before upload.
Review retention settings for conversation logs.
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive workflows to a local-only deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or network capabilities and is not runnable, while Dify has filesystem write and shell execution but modify_git_state is false. There is no overlapping mutable resource shown in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is limited; uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not expose a shared writable directory.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory outside the documented sandbox
IF an operator manually copies outputs between them into shared files
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Do not mount the same volume into both systems.
Use read-only imports for awesome-selfhosted content.
Avoid git-based workflows for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add OS-level filesystem isolation.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can act on agent outputs through workflows and tools, so if awesome-selfhosted content is used as a source of facts, Dify may render or operationalize it without verification. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source, not an executor, so the cascade is from reference content into Dify’s action layer rather than between two active agents.
conditions: IF Dify workflows consume awesome-selfhosted-derived text as authoritative input
IF downstream tools or agents execute actions based on that text without validation
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking tool.
Mark imported reference content as non-authoritative.
Require citations for any generated recommendation.
Limit workflows to read-only summarization.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes, while Dify handles knowledge-base content and conversation logs; the only compliance concern visible is generic logging/retention exposure, which is lower severity absent a regulated data class or jurisdictional mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF the deployment’s retention policy is longer than the operator’s policy
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Dify.
Set short log retention.
Review export/delete procedures.
Separate public reference content from private workflows.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
